plan: BELOW-MARKET LADDER + POST-Q3 EVIDENCE GATE. Nothing at market, nothing above $19.75, and the principal stages it - nothing rests without the principal. Deliberately written as TWO ALTERNATIVE branches rather than an AND-gate, because price and evidence are negatively correlated here (if Q3 confirms, the stock will not be at $19.75) and an AND-gate would be an unfillable 'no' dressed up as a plan. Full size = 0.75% of the $3.3M deployable base = ~$25k (the 1.2% ruled cap cut for the business-risk finding per the response taxonomy), split across the branches. BRANCH A (below-market GTC ladder, pre-Q3, half size ~$12.5k): nothing above $19.75 - Icahn's verified $19.74 average basis on 11.85M shares and the top of the 2025 SWX distribution band ($17.50-$21.50). Three GTC rungs: $19.75 x 40% (~253sh), $18.25 x 35% (~241sh), $17.00 x 25% (~182sh); cancel-and-review 2 sessions before the Q3 print. BRANCH B (evidence-led, post-Q3, the other ~$12.5k plus any unfilled Branch A): opens only if the Q3 FY26 print (expected ~2026-11-04) delivers Q3 base gross profit margin >=8.8% AND no cut to the $270M FY26 base gross profit floor, subject to a valuation ceiling of EV/forward adj EBITDA <=11.0x at the post-print price. If the Q3 evidence FAILS (base GPM <8.5% or guidance cut) BOTH branches close and the name is dead for this cycle, including any Branch A fills, which get re-courted for exit.

edge_explainer: The -21.5% is a genuine DE-RATE, not a derailment - revenue guidance rose $300M and adj EBITDA guidance rose $2.5M, and EV/FY26E adj EBITDA went 12.0x to 10.0x on a raise. But the de-rate is CORRECT, so there is no price edge. What the market repriced is revenue QUALITY, and the primary sources back it: H1-26 operating income was FLAT at $19.407M vs $19.446M on +$411M (+32%) of revenue; the company raised revenue guidance $300M for $10M of gross profit (a 3.3% incremental margin); and the implied full-year base gross margin guide was CUT 40bps (8.18% to 7.78%) inside a release headlined 'RAISES GUIDANCE'. The structural fact underneath: 77% of revenue is unit-price plus fixed-price - the contractor bears cost inflation - with escalators that reset ANNUALLY and are CAPPED, and the 10-Q concedes 'our actual costs at times can exceed the contractual caps'. So the $6M fuel hit is not recoverable inside FY26, and the guide assumes elevated fuel only through Q3. Mix is compounding it: US Gas went from 46.5% to 50.9% of revenue at a 5.95% base margin, and bid work went from 17.6% to 25.0% of revenue since FY23. The seed's bull leg - 'H2 9.0% vs H1 6.3% is normal seasonality' - does NOT survive the quarterly history: Q1 is the trough (GAAP GPM 6.42/2.51/3.70/4.94% in FY23/24/25/26) while Q2-Q4 blend to 9.3-10.3%, so Q2-26's 7.90% base is a 100bps y/y miss IN the normal band, and H2 must snap back to ~9.0% in one quarter. Three seed claims REFUTED on primary sources: the Southwest Gas overhang is GONE (zero shares since 2025-09-05, Tax Matters Agreement restrictions terminated) - but 11.47M registered, unlocked ICAHN resale shares (11.4% of shares out) replaced it, and he can sell 8.9M and keep his board seat; today's $21.88 is ABOVE Icahn's verified $19.74 average, not below; and the 'Icahn added $78M in March 2026' headline is a mark-to-market artifact - the S-3ASR and proxy show the position unchanged at 14,336,044. Four bear claims also REFUTED: H1 CFO -$15.0M is seasonal (H1-25 was -$11.0M; identical at -0.89% vs -0.86% of revenue; FY25 CFO +$78.1M with Q4 alone +$83.9M); receivables are in line (AR+contract assets +33.8% vs revenue +32.3%) and the Chicago item is a fully-written-off 2019-vintage municipal claim; covenant risk is remote (2.6x vs a 4.00x step-down from Q3-26); and the Non-Union Electric 'margin collapse' is a storm-revenue artifact (base margin actually improved FY24 ~4.2% to FY25 ~8.2%). The takeaway-vs-data divergence is real but every datum is disclosed and the market priced all of it the same session - disclosed and instantly priced means no honesty alpha, only a diligence edge. AI-BREAK conflict: the entry does NOT require the cycle holding - 59.4% of revenue (US Gas + Canadian LDC replacement) is mandate-driven and AI-independent, and the 40.6% Electric half is exposed only at the second derivative through rate-based utility capex. Direct datacenter exposure is small and new ($125M award = 2% of backlog, plus JJ White's unweighted $2.8B pipeline), but it is where the GROWTH narrative is pivoting, so a break mostly kills the bull case rather than creating new downside. discovery_state DISCOVERING/CROWDED: $2.2B NYSE name, JPM Sell $26 and Cantor $37.40 published, ~33% of float in four hands (Icahn 14.2%, Vanguard 7.9%, BlackRock 6.6% and adding, Fidelity 5.0%), short interest only 3.78% of float at 2.03 days to cover - no squeeze fuel. Net: +9.1% to expected fair value with a 35% probability of $17, 2.6x leverage, a management frame that has failed twice in 90 days, a float distributed at $17.50-$21.50 within the last twelve months, and a fresh 26-week low closing at the low of the day - against a decisive datapoint that is dated and only three months away. There is no reason to pay for that option today. PEER RULING (recomputed at the 2026-08-04 close on one convention): the cohort median is 18.28x EV/EBITDA and CTRI sits at ~12.9x on the same basis - but the naive 'deeply cheap' read is REJECTED. Every expensive name in the set is an electric/power/datacenter story (PWR 36.1x, IESC 26.8x, MTZ 18.9x, DY 18.3x, ECG 18.2x) and the only two cheap ones are the two without it (PRIM 10.8x, CTRI ~12.9x). CTRI's discount to the cohort IS the AI-capex premium it does not carry, so owning it for multiple convergence is a levered bet on the AI cycle holding - the opposite of what a 51%-gas revenue mix makes it look like. What the peer work DID correct: my first-pass 10.0x base multiple was PRIM's deteriorating-name mark (PRIM is the only peer with declining revenue, -5.4%) applied to a company growing 33%; MTZ carries the same ~8% margin and gets 18.9x on +23% growth. Base re-struck at 11.0x, taking E[FV] from $23.95 to $26.31 and the edge from +9.1% to +19.8%, and the verdict from 4/10 to 5/10. The residual discount is earned: second-highest leverage in the cohort (~3.0x on the peer EBITDA convention), second-lowest EBITDA margin (~6.8%), margins compressing while the cohort's expand, a two-year public history, and 77% unit/fixed-price exposure.
response_taxonomy: Two-class finding. VALUATION (the multiple) -> price gate, the one case where a price gate is the correct instrument. BUSINESS RISK (contract mix, incremental margin structure) -> SIZE cut, not a price gate. Decisive evidence is DATED (Q3 print ~2026-11-04) -> tranche behind the gate rather than stage now. All three applied: price gate $19.75, size cut 1.2% -> 0.75%, three-rung tranche.
